s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with vomiting and abdominal pain in the context of fasting and marked weight loss
salient_findings: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs showed marked gastric distension
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum
No intrinsic luminal lesions found on endoscopy

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with vomiting and abdominal pain in the context of fasting and marked weight loss
salient_findings: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta
key_facts: Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
Abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs showed marked gastric distension
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum
No intrinsic luminal lesions found on endoscopy

differentials: Desmoid tumor of the small intestine
per_call: Desmoid tumor of the small intestine

shortlist.label: Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle

shortlist.label: Duodenal Stenosis
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum and postprandial upper abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar mechanism of compression as Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome

shortlist.label: Gastroparesis
shortlist.why_kept: Intractable vomiting and bloating in the context of marked weight loss and fasting

raw.rationale: The contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle, which is a hallmark of Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome. The patient's marked leanness and compliance with fasting customs also support this diagnosis, as weight loss can exacerbate the condition.

rejected.label: Gastric Outlet Obstruction
rejected.why: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was normal, with no intrinsic luminal lesions found, making an obstruction less likely

rejected.label: Duodenal Stenosis
rejected.why: The absence of intrinsic luminal lesions on endoscopy and the specific finding of duodenal compression by the superior mesenteric artery on CT make stenosis less likely

rejected.label: Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves compression of the celiac artery, not the duodenum, and does not match the CT findings

rejected.label: Gastroparesis
rejected.why: While gastroparesis could explain some symptoms like vomiting and bloating, the specific finding of duodenal compression on CT and the lack of other diagnostic evidence for gastroparesis make it less likely
